1. **A local command's own echo confirms its send.** A driver's `send` of a local slash command that the CLI runs
   reads as delivered (`ok`), confirmed by an echo of that command the product can observe, never presumed; a local
   command the CLI did not run is never confirmed by it. Today a local command outside the compiled list

   `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted` after its window although it ran; a listed command with no measured
   post-condition (or on an unverified CLI) reads `ok` with `confirmed: false`, detail `unconfirmable`.

2. **The echo is measured, not assumed.** `[inferred]` What «echo» the CLI gives for a local command that the product
   can observe (a hook event, a screen line the vt100 readiness model already reads, or another signal) is unknown at
   take-up; P3 re-measures it from the code and the recorded fixtures (`fixtures/claude/<version>/`), and which
   commands it covers, before the plan states it (the directive's item 1, inputs#I1). Every dependence on an
   undocumented `claude` behaviour is a capability-ledger row with a `viola verify` probe (CLAUDE.md Critical
   Warnings), so an echo the product relies on is a ledger row, measured and stamped, or the send stays honest about
   what it cannot confirm.

3. **What a send of a local command reads today, re-measured.** `[inferred]` The three readings above (the listed
   post-conditions, `unconfirmable`, and the unlisted command's `no-prompt-submitted`) are read from the code at
   take-up; P3 confirms them against `src/run/send.rs`, `src/run/send/classify.rs`, the CLI `send` human mirror
   (`src/human/mirror.rs`, `unconfirmable`'s fixed note) and the MCP `send` result, and what the driver sees for each.

4. **Capability this chunk addresses:** `v2-23` (a send of a local slash command that runs reads as delivered,
   confirmed by the command's own echo). The claim is decided at P5.

7. **The echo read** — new `src/run/send/echo.rs`, the root binary's: `end_of(path) -> Option<u64>` and

- Answers `--version` like the real CLI. Standing as `hyprctl` by its own file name (in a test-scoped bin dir, in place of the real `hyprctl`; viola-hyprland's own unit tests serve `hyprctl` by a planted shell stub instead, because cargo-mutants runs only the mutated package's tests, so a root-package test cannot kill that crate's mutants), it reads its mode and reply set from files beside its exe, never from the env. It reads hook commands from `<plugin-dir>/hooks/hooks.json` (the `--plugin-dir` `run` passes). Only an absolute exec-form `command` is spawned: no shell, no PATH; a group's `matcher` is evaluated against a tool-bearing payload's `tool_name` (`hook_commands(…, tool)`). A non-absolute command is receipted `command_absolute:false, ran:false` and never run. The payload is `<fixtures>/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json`, with only `prompt` set for UserPromptSubmit and the fixture's trailing newline kept, so the recorded prompt yields the recorded bytes; under `--resume <id>` the launch SessionStart is the set's recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` when the set holds it (2.1.287, 2.1.302), else its recorded `SessionStart.default` (a set without the variant, 2.1.288), with `source` `resume` and `session_id` the id given (with `--fork-session`, the compiled fork id), and no other payload is built save the compact replay's `SessionStart.compact-1` under `--framing`, whose `session_id` is set to the last SessionStart the agent fired, and under `--transcript` the launch SessionStart's `transcript_path`.

Exits on `\x03` or at stdin EOF, first waiting for a hook still running and starting no other; on Unix every command it spawns (each hook) runs in a process group of its own (`process_group(0)`, as the `--exit-no-eof` holder does), because a hangup of its PTY's foreground group, at its exit as session leader or when a killed wrapper closes the PTY, cuts a `viola hook` short in its exit-time coverage write (a cut-short profile, measured); the agent itself, its PTY's session leader, cannot leave that group (`setpgid` refuses a leader), so on Unix its exit ignores SIGHUP from its first step (`\x03` or stdin's end): a hangup that lands while it exits (a killed wrapper, or portable-pty's SIGHUP-first kill) no longer cuts its own exit-time coverage write, and one that lands before the exit begins still ends it (measured). That exit, shared Unix code, is witnessed on Linux only: `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs` `fake_agent_exit_outlives_a_hangup_that_lands_while_it_exits` (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`) reads the SIGHUP disposition through `ps -o sigignore= -p <pid>`; it runs on CI's one leg, `ubuntu-latest`.
